messages:
acme_ops: hey team — started seeing JSON parse errors in prod after we bumped the model yesterday. ~5% of invoices failing when we call json_mode. parser throws 'Unexpected token' and points to 'Note:' text. full sample below.
maya_support: thanks for flagging — can you paste the raw response (exact bytes) and the request id? also which model + params did you use? we'll triage and escalate if needed. :eyes:
acme_ops: request_id=rid_0a9f3b2c, model=open-llama-13b-v2, temp=0.0, max_output_tokens=600, streaming=true, json_mode=true. reproducer (curl):

```
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.inference/v1/completions \ 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \ 
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ 
  -d '{
    "model":"open-llama-13b-v2",
    "prompt":"Generate invoice JSON for order...",
    "json_mode":true,
    "max_output_tokens":600,
    "temperature":0
  }'
```

here's the exact chunk we got (trimmed):

```
{"invoice_id":"INV-98123","items":[{"sku":"A1","qty":2}],"total":123.45
Note: customer requested expedited shipping, billed separately
```

parser fails because extra plaintext is appended after JSON and closing brace sometimes dropped. This started ~2026-03-01 after model rollout. Impact: downstream ETL fails, customer-facing queue backs up. urgent.

maya_support: got it — sharing with eng. quick workaround: set streaming=false for now (forces server to return full payload) or add a robust post-parse step that attempts to recover by trimming trailing non-JSON and ensuring a closing brace. also try lowering max_output_tokens to a conservative number so the model finishes before chunk boundary. can you try streaming=false and report? :pray:

oncall-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-1354 — escalated to eng-ml, SLA target 48h for enterprise impact.

acme_ops: tried streaming=false — reduced failure rate but still see ~0.5% malformed responses (rare). post-parse fix is heavy for us. we need a permanent fix or rollback to previous model. customer contracts mention 99.9% structured output availability.

maya_support: understood. @devin_engineer — can you take a look? attaching request_id above and a raw chunk. we suspect streaming chunk termination may be dropping final tokens or not guaranteeing final flush of whitespace boundaries.

devin_engineer: looking now. initial hunch: when streaming is enabled we emit chunked deltas; if a token boundary contains only the final '}' the chunker might be lost at backpressure drop. will repro locally with same tokenizer + streaming flag. can you share the full encoded bytes (base64) for that request_id so I can inspect chunk boundaries? also tagging @sre-bot for network traces.

acme_ops: attaching base64 payload in support ticket (sent). also we observed this with two different models (open-llama-13b-v2 and a trimmed-rerun), but started after the rollout date above.

sre-bot: collected network logs for rid_0a9f3b2c — no downstream connection resets. observed final chunk length 0 for stream close event at 2026-03-01T14:02:11Z — correlating with client disconnects. forwarding to eng-runtime.

devin_engineer: repro'd locally with streaming + simulated client disconnect — confirmed boundary behavior where final token is omitted if client-side stream EOF races with server flush. root cause: server flush path wasn't guaranteed to append the final buffered tokens when stream state transitions to 'close' under high concurrency. creating PR to always flush final buffer and emit explicit end-of-stream sentinel ("\n__END_JSON__\n") for streaming clients that opt-in. will add metrics and a canary rollout.

maya_support: thanks @devin_engineer. plan: 1) immediate: recommend customers set streaming=false or apply post-parse repair rule; 2) next 24h: deploy fix behind a feature flag + canary, monitor; 3) 48h: full rollout if canary stable. SLA note: we'll treat this as P2 for enterprise customers and communicate ETA to affected customers. I'll draft comms.

acme_ops: appreciated. two asks: can you (a) provide us a temporary option to force server to append an explicit end marker so we can detect truncation (we'll patch our parser), and (b) notify when canary starts so we can validate with a test harness?

devin_engineer: yes — adding a query param streaming_end_marker=true that will append the sentinel string on stream termination for canary customers. ETA test canary in ~6 hours. will ping here when live and include a sample test prompt.

maya_support: flagged INC-2026-1354 with customer impact and tentative ETA. @acme_ops I'll DM you the test harness URL and the canary flag to flip. once validated we can coordinate rollback if any regression.

acme_ops: thanks all — we can test as soon as canary ready. appreciate the quick triage. :heart:

sre-bot: Canary deployment started 2026-03-02T20:10:00Z for streaming-end-marker feature. monitoring logs for truncated-json errors.

devin_engineer: canary shows 0 occurrences in initial 2h window for the same repro prompts. rolling to 10% traffic in 3h, full rollout 24h if stable. PR #3128 includes tests and the sentinel opt-in.

maya_support: messaging plan: email to affected customers with postmortem and interim workarounds + invite to validate canary. SLA note: targeted resolution within 48h, compensatory usage credit discussed per contract. will keep thread updated.

acme_ops: validated canary — sentinel appended and our parser detected the marker. thank you. please keep us posted on full rollout timing.

maya_support: closing loop: marking INC-2026-1354 as mitigated after canary success. follow-up: postmortem will include root cause, fix, and recommended client-side defensive parsing patterns. will share when ready. :white_check_mark:
